hero.lead: Your films and series, in one place. A small server at home. A native player on your desktop. No account. No telemetry.
hero.note: One maintainer. Windows x64 is the only platform used with a real household library so far.

v5.title: Everything you own, in one library.
v5.lead: Your computers, your NAS and your cloud become a single library, with one profile that follows you from one to the other.
v5.promise: A target, not a promise: Theia 5 is published only when its final checks pass.

features.title: One library, many places
features.body: Films, Series, Search and Home combine your computers, NAS folders and cloud. A small line says where each copy lives.

features.title: One profile that follows you
features.body: Link your profile across your servers. What you watched and where you stopped follows you from one server to the next.

features.title: Google Drive as a source
features.body: Stream from the Drive folders you choose, in short pieces. Until Google approves Theia's own connection, connecting may ask for your own Google client.

features.title: NAS folders
features.body: A NAS share mounted on a server joins the library, and your history survives if it sleeps. The UGREEN test kit is unverified on a real UGREEN so far.

features.title: Servers and sources, in settings
features.body: Add, rename and reconnect servers and sources on one settings page, each with a small icon: tower, laptop, NAS or cloud. Pair a machine with a short code.

features.title: One page for every title
features.body: The same title page whichever source holds the file: play, resume, mark as watched, leave an opinion and preview a scene.

features.title: Watched means watched
features.body: Anti-spoil shows an episode's artwork once you pass its last fifth, and a file's own ending-credits chapter counts as watched.

features.title: An update that keeps everything
features.body: Upgrading from 4.4.6 keeps your library, profiles and history. Checked on a real 4.4.6 installation, rollback included.

v5.laterIntro: Planned, but not promised for this release. Each one is announced once it is proven on real hardware.

later.title: An Android app
later.body: A phone app for your server or your sources. Not started yet; planned after the desktop release.

later.title: Android TV and Google TV
later.body: Casting or an app on the TV: the living room is still being studied.

later.title: ARM computers
later.body: Native Windows and Linux ARM64 apps, announced only once built and checked. Older ARM64 setups stay labelled as earlier versions.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: No account and no telemetry. This page says exactly what leaves your computer, to whom and why, and what never does.
privacy.stays: Your library catalogue, your viewing history and your files. Theia does not upload them.
privacy.tmdb: Looks up posters, synopses and cast for the titles in your library. Results are kept on your computer.
privacy.github: Checks for updates and downloads them from the project's releases.
privacy.firebase: Runs the friends service: friend codes, profile photos, presence and opinions, through an anonymous sign-in. It connects while your server runs.
privacy.remote: Remote viewing connects your own devices directly, over WireGuard. No relay and no control plane sit in between.
privacy.drive: Theia 5 can read video files from Google Drive folders you choose. You sign in on Google's own page, so Theia never sees your Google password. The authorisation stays on the computer that runs your Theia server, and Theia only lists and streams the files you allowed, to your own devices. Nothing is sent to the maintainer. You can disconnect Drive in Theia, or revoke access in your Google account, at any time.
privacy.site: No cookies, no analytics and no remote resources. Your language choice stays in this browser. The host, like any web host, sees visitors' IP addresses in its own server logs.

faq.title: Good questions.
faq.intro: Straight answers before you press play. Need a hand? Find us on GitHub or Discord.

items.question: Does Theia come with films or series?
items.answer: No. Theia organises and plays video files you already have and are entitled to use. It is not a streaming catalogue and does not supply films. Posters, synopses and cast come from TMDB and are cached locally.

items.question: Is it free? Is the source public?
items.answer:
The server, library, ordinary viewing and every V4 feature are free for personal, non-commercial use. Nothing paid exists. Any future paid features, if introduced, will be announced beforehand.

Releases from 4.0 use PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; source code is developed privately and is not published. Version 3.4.0 and earlier remain GPL-3.0 with their source at the public tags. Commercial use requires a separate licence.

items.question: Which systems are supported, and what is actually tested?
items.answer:
Desktop setups exist for Windows, macOS and Ubuntu 24.04. Windows x64 is the only platform used with the maintainer's real library. The bundled 4.4.2 players passed generated-film checks on Windows, Linux x64 and hosted Macs, with Intel under Rosetta; this does not establish your screen or audio chain. Older ARM64 downloads are labelled explicitly.

Linux uses software decoding, SDR and PCM. macOS uses PCM; physical-display HDR and hardware decoding are unverified. Windows requests bitstream and falls back to PCM, but delivery of Atmos or DTS-HD MA to a receiver remains unverified. The browser viewer remains available on phones and TVs without active playback development.

items.question: Which processor should I choose?
items.answer: On Windows, open Settings → System → About and read System type: Intel/AMD means x64; an ARM processor means ARM64. On macOS, About This Mac lists either an Apple chip or an Intel processor. On Ubuntu, uname -m returns x86_64 for x64 or aarch64 for ARM64. The site selects the system only; you choose the processor.

items.question: How do I install or update Theia?
items.answer:
Download the setup for your system and processor. Choose the language, whether this computer serves, plays or does both, and your media folders. Start Theia from your launcher or with theia. On macOS and Ubuntu, make the setup executable first. Ubuntu also needs the listed desktop prerequisites.

For an update, run the new setup: your library and progress are kept. The setup and application currently support English and French, independently of this site's language.

items.question: What stays private? What leaves my computer?
items.answer:
No cloud account and no telemetry. Theia uses three external services: TMDB for film and series metadata and artwork; GitHub Releases for updates; and Firebase Realtime Database (project theia-friends, with anonymous sign-in and token renewal) solely for the friends service: friend codes, profile photos, requests, presence and opinions.

Firebase connects when the server starts and follows its inbox. It publishes directory entries for all local profiles, even before you add a friend: friend-code identifiers, names, the server public key, local profile numbers and port; photos are uploaded separately. Linked friends exchange presence, which can include the current title, episode details and artwork paths, room invitations, server version and direct tunnel addresses. You can hide the title and last-seen time. Invisible hides activity, titles, room offers and last-seen time; it does not disconnect Firebase or remove directory entries and photos. Opinions remain in recipients' inboxes until deleted or the friendship ends. Your library catalogue and viewing history are not uploaded.

Anyone who can reach port 8383 on your network can browse and administer Theia. Use a trusted network and never forward that port to the internet. This website has no analytics, remote embeds or cookies; an explicit language choice is stored only in this browser.

items.question: How do friends, rooms and remote access work?
items.answer:
Exchange friend codes, then invite friends into a private room. Remote access uses device keys and direct WireGuard connections, without a media relay or control plane. Discovery, presence and opinions use Firebase. Connectivity depends on your networks.

The maintainer reported a working two-household test session, but private rooms and the shared countdown still lack a complete real two-household validation. There is no live TV, DVR, music library, plugin system or multi-user permissions.

items.question: Where can I get help or report a problem?
items.answer: Join the project's Discord or open a GitHub issue. Include your version, system, processor and what happened. For a playback problem, add the file's video/audio formats. Share what worked, too. Never post credentials or a private library publicly; report security issues through the repository's security policy.
